the 17th to the 19th centuries, political entities in the area included the [[Kingdom of Dahomey]], the city-state of [[Porto-Novo#History|Porto Novo]], and other states to the north. France took over the territory in 1894, incorporating it into [[French West Africa]] as [[French Dahomey]]. In 1960, Dahomey gained full independence from France. As a [[sovereign state]], Benin has had [[democratic governments]], [[military coup]]s, and [[military government]]s. A self-described [[Marxist–Leninist state]] called the [[People's Republic of Benin]] existed between 1975 and 1990. In 1991, it was replaced by the [[Multi-party system|multi-party]] Republic of Benin.{{cite book |title=Global Logistics Assessments Reports Handbook |volume=1: Strategic Transportation and Customs Information for Selected Countries |publisher=International Business Publications USA |date=2008 |orig-date=2015 |isbn=978-0-7397-6603-3 |page=85 }} The [[official language]] of Benin is French, with indigenous languages such as [[Fon language|Fon]], [[Bariba language|Bariba]], [[Yoruba language|Yoruba]] and [[Dendi language|Dendi]] also spoken. The largest religious group in Benin, as projected for 2020 by the [[Pew Research Center|Pew Research Centre]] in 2026 based on 2010 statistics, is [[Christianity]] (53%), followed by [[Islam]] (31%) and other faiths including [[African traditional religion]]s (11%).{{Cite web |last=Tong|first=Yunping|date=12 February 2026|title=Religious Diversity Around the World|url=https://www.pewresearch.org/religion/2026/02/12/religious-diversity-around-the-world/|access-date=16 July 2026|website=[[Pew Research Center]]|language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Hackett|first=Conrad|last2=Stonawski|first2=Marcin|last3=Tong|first3=Yunping|last4=Kramer|first4=Stephanie|last5=Shi|first5=Anne|last6=Fahmy|first6=Dalia|date=9 June 2025|title=14. The seat of the [[province of Bergamo]], it is located approximately {{convert|40|km|0|abbr=on}} northeast of [[Milan]], and about {{convert|30|km|0|abbr=on}} from the [[alpine lake]]s [[Lake Como|Como]] and [[Lake Iseo|Iseo]] and {{convert|70|km|0|abbr=on}} from [[Lake Garda|Garda]] and [[Lake Maggiore|Maggiore]]. The [[Bergamo Alps]] ({{lang|it|Alpi Orobie}}) begin immediately north of the city. With a population of 120,629 as of 2026, Bergamo is the [[List of municipalities of Lombardy|4th-largest city in Lombardy]] and the [[List of cities in Italy|34th-largest in Italy]]. The [[metropolitan area]] of Bergamo extends beyond the administrative city limits, spanning over a densely urbanized area with slightly fewer than 500,000 inhabitants.{{cite web |url=http://www.cityrailways.it/storage/pdf/01_urbanismi%20ITALIA_2011.pdf|title=Urbanismi in Italia, 2011 |website=cityrailways.it |language=Italian |trans-title=|access-date=4 November 2014}} The Bergamo metropolitan area is itself part of the broader [[Milan metropolitan area]], home to more than eight million people.{{cite web |url=https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2016/12/oecd-territorial-reviews-bergamo-italy_g1g6470b/9789264251984-en.pdf |title= OECD Territorial Reviews: Bergamo, Italy |author= Davide Cappellini |date= 2016 |publisher= OECD |page= 63 |ISBN= 978-92-64-25198-4 |access-date=23 October 2025 |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20251023140918/https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2016/12/oecd-territorial-reviews-bergamo-italy_g1g6470b/9789264251984-en.pdf |archive-date=23 October 2025 }}{{cite web |url=http://urbact.eu/fileadmin/subsites/Metrogov/pdf/Milan_s2.pdf |title=Competitiveness and knowledge transfer |access-date=22 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205140422/http://urbact.eu/fileadmin/subsites/Metrogov/pdf/Milan_s2.pdf |archive-date=5 December 2008 }} Competitiveness of Milan and its metropolitan area[http://demo.istat.it/bilmens2013gen/index.html ISTAT] The city of Bergamo is composed of an old walled core, known as {{lang|it|Città Alta}} ('Upper Town'), nestled within a [[Parco dei Colli di Bergamo|system of hills]], and the modern expansion in the plains below. The upper town is encircled by massive [[Republic of Venice|Venetian]] [[Venetian Works of Defence between 15th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar|defensive systems]] that have been a [[UNESCO World Heritage Site]] since 9 July 2017.{{Cite web|url=http://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/331/|title=The city of Bergamo - UNESCO World Heritage Centre|last=Centre|first=UNESCO World Heritage|website=whc.unesco.org|language=en|access-date=2 November 2017}} Bergamo has good links to other cities in Italy via the [[autostrada A4|motorway A4]] which connects Milan, [[Verona]], and [[Venice]]. The city is served by [[Il Caravaggio International Airport]], the third-busiest airport in Italy with 12.3 million passengers in 2017. Bergamo is the second most visited city in Lombardy after Milan.{{cite web|url=http://www.asr-lombardia.it/RSY/tourism/flows-of-tourists/lombardia-and-provinces/tables/12193/2012/|title=RSY Lombardia-Arrivals and nights spent by guests in accommodation establishments, by type of resort and by type of establishment. Total accommodation establishments. Part III. Tourist resort. Year 2012|publisher=asr-lombardia.it|access-date=4 November 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104173830/http://www.asr-lombardia.it/RSY/tourism/flows-of-tourists/lombardia-and-provinces/tables/12193/2012/|archive-date=4 November 2014}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.ecodibergamo.it/stories/bergamo-citta/lombardia-pil-piu-alto-in-italiabergamodead-u-disoccupazione-ai-minimi_1233033_11/|title=Lombardia, Pil più alto in Italia Bergamo disoccupazione ai minimi|access-date=11 October 2017|language=it}}

The club's football team is one of the [[Big Three (Turkey)|Big Three]] in [[Turkey]] and one of the most successful teams in the country, having never been relegated to a lower division. It was the first registered sports club in the country and one of the few that acquired the right to bear the [[Flag of Turkey|Turkish flag]] on its crest. Its football team has won 21 league titles including 16 [[Süper Lig|Turkish Süper Lig]], three [[Turkish National Division]] and two [[Turkish Football Championship]] titles, along with 11 [[Turkish Cup]] titles. Beşiktaş is also the only team to have won the Süper Lig undefeated, in the [[1991–92 1.Lig|1991–92 campaign]]. The team last won the Turkish [[Süper Lig]] title during the [[2020–21 Süper Lig|2020–21 season]] and the Turkish Cup in the [[2023–24 Süper Lig|2023–24 season]]. The club's home ground is [[Beşiktaş Stadium]], a 42,684-capacity [[all-seater stadium]] located by [[Dolmabahçe Palace]]. The stadium has been considered one of the best in the world for location, design, comfort, technology, atmosphere, and transportation.{{cite news |title=Vodafone Park wins Stadium Project of the Year |url=https://turkish-football.com/liverpool-fc-las-vegas-project-pipped-by-the-besiktas-vodafone-park-for-stadium-project-of-the-year-award/ |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Turkish-Football.com |publisher=Turkish Football |language=en}} The team also participates in European competitions regularly. Beşiktaş reached the quarter-finals of the [[1986–87 European Cup]] and displayed the best Turkish team performance in the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage by earning 14 points and progressing undefeated in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18]] campaign. Beşiktaş have also reached the [[UEFA Europa League]]{{efn|Known as [[UEFA Cup]] until [[2008–09 UEFA Cup|2008–09 season]].}} quarter-finals twice, in the [[2002–03 UEFA Cup|2002–03]] and [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League|2016–17]] seasons. Based on its [[UEFA coefficient]], Beşiktaş is currently the 4th highest ranked Turkish team and is ranked third all-time after its rivals [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] and [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]].{{Cite web |title=Club coefficients: UEFA rankings |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/uefarankings/club/?year=2026 |access-date=2024-04-17 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}} The club's fan base, [[Çarşı (supporter group)|Çarşı]], is well known globally.{{cite magazine |last=Batuman |first=Elif |date=7 March 2011 |title=The View from the Stands |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2011/03/07/the-view-from-the-stands |access-date=9 August 2025 |department=Letter from Turkey |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en}} They were chosen as the best fan group in voting conducted by American sports viewers due to their 132-decibel noise record at a 2007 match against [[Liverpool FC|Liverpool]].{{cite web |title=What makes round of 16 debutants Beşiktaş special? |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5116bc76b4-25dec61dbf40-1000--what-makes-round-of-16-debutants-besiktas-special/ |access-date=9 August 2025 |website=UEFA |language=en}} The group is involved with sociopolitical causes and is traditionally considered to be working-class and left-wing, supporting what is known as "the people's team".{{Cite news|last=McManus|first=John|date=2009-11-24|title=Besiktas fans reveal united front|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8376619.stm|access-date=2021-06-27}} The highest ever football attendance in Turkish league history was recorded in a [[Beşiktaş–Galatasaray rivalry|Beşiktaş–Galatasaray derby]] with 76,127 spectators.{{cite news |title=Atatürk Olimpiyat Stadı'nda seyirci rekoru |url=https://www.sozcu.com.tr/ataturk-olimpiyat-stadinda-seyirci-rekoru-wp376377 |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Sözcü |language=tr}}{{cite news |title=Beşiktaş–Galatasaray derbisinde 76 bin 127 seyirci |url=https://www.milliyet.com.tr/skorer/besiktas-galatasaray-derbisinde-76-bin-127-seyirci-2564835 |access-date=9 August 2025 |work=Milliyet |language=tr}} The club also competes in other sports such as [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|men's]], [[Beşiktaş JK (women's basketball)|women's]] and [[Beşiktaş JK (wheelchair basketball)|wheelchair]]), volleyball ([[Beşiktaş JK (men's volleyball)|men's]] and [[Beşiktaş JK (women's volleyball)|women's]]), [[Beşiktaş JK (handball)|handball]], [[Beşiktaş J.K. (athletics)|athletics]], beach football, boxing, bridge, chess, gymnastics, athletics, parasports, rowing, table tennis, wrestling and [[esports]].{{cite web |title=Hakkında |url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/cms/hakkinda/1/ |access-date=9 August 2025 |website=Beşiktaş JK |publisher=Beşiktaş Jimnastik Kulübü |language=tr}}

References:{{cite web |url=https://www.boeing.com/company/general-info/#/employment-data |publisher=Boeing |title=General Information |access-date=March 25, 2024 }} }} '''The Boeing Company''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|b|oʊ|ɪ|ŋ}} {{respell|BO|ing}}) is an American [[multinational corporation]] that designs and manufactures [[airplane]]s, [[rotorcraft]], [[rocket]]s, [[satellite]]s, and [[missile]]s worldwide.{{Cite web |last=Bernal |first=Kyle |date=December 23, 2022 |title=What Are the Top Boeing Government Contracts? |url=https://executivegov.com/articles/what-are-the-top-boeing-government-contracts |website=executivegov.com |access-date=June 8, 2023 |language=en-US |archive-date=June 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230614003732/https://executivegov.com/articles/what-are-the-top-boeing-government-contracts/ |url-status=live}} The company also provides leasing and product support services. Boeing is among the largest global [[aerospace manufacturer]]s; it is the fourth-largest [[List of defense contractors|defense contractor]] in the world based on 2022 revenue{{Cite web |title=The SIPRI Top 100 arms-producing and military services companies in the world, 2022 |publisher=SIPRI |url=https://www.sipri.org/visualizations/2023/sipri-top-100-arms-producing-and-military-services-companies-world-2022 |access-date=2024-02-16 |language=en |archive-date=March 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240307215359/https://www.sipri.org/visualizations/2023/sipri-top-100-arms-producing-and-military-services-companies-world-2022 |url-status=live}} and is the largest exporter in the United States by dollar value.{{Cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/money/industries/manufacturing/2009-03-25-boeing-recession_N.htm |title=Boeing says it's flying high despite recession |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111124655/http://www.usatoday.com/money/industries/manufacturing/2009-03-25-boeing-recession_N.htm |archive-date=January 11, 2012 |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=March 27, 2009}} Boeing was founded in 1916 by [[William E. Boeing]] in [[Seattle]], Washington.{{cite web |url=https://www.boeing.com/resources/boeingdotcom/history/pdf/Boeing_Chronology.pdf |title=Boeing history chronology |website=Boeing |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180508151641/http://www.boeing.com/resources/boeingdotcom/history/pdf/Boeing_Chronology.pdf |archive-date=May 8, 2018 |url-status=live}} The present corporation is the result of the Boeing acquisition of [[McDonnell Douglas]] on August 1, 1997. The Boeing Company's corporate headquarters is located in the [[Crystal City, Virginia|Crystal City]] neighborhood of [[Arlington County, Virginia]], near [[Washington, DC]].{{cite web |last=Hansen |first=Drew |date=February 21, 2023|work=Washington Business Journal |title=Boeing offers CEO Dave Calhoun more than $5M in additional stock awards to stay on |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/washington/news/2023/02/21/boeing-dave-calhoun-compensation.html |access-date=April 9, 2023 |archive-date=May 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514152138/https://www.bizjournals.com/washington/news/2023/02/21/boeing-dave-calhoun-compensation.html |url-status=live}} The company is organized into three primary divisions: [[Boeing Commercial Airplanes]] (BCA), [[Boeing Defense, Space & Security]] (BDS), and [[Boeing Global Services]] (BGS). In 2021, Boeing recorded $62.3{{nbsp}}billion in sales.{{cite web |url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/264374/boeings-worldwide-revenue/ |title=Boeing's worldwide revenue from FY 2007 to FY 2021 |date=February 3, 2023 |publisher=Statista |access-date=April 25, 2023 |archive-date=April 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427043714/https://www.statista.com/statistics/264374/boeings-worldwide-revenue/ |url-status=live}} Boeing is ranked 54th on the [[Fortune 500|''Fortune'' 500]] list (2020),{{cite web |url=http://fortune.com/fortune500/boeing/ |title=Boeing |website=Fortune |language=en-US |access-date=July 22, 2021 |archive-date=June 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170630173450/http://fortune.com/fortune500/boeing/ |url-status=live}} and ranked 121st on the [[Fortune Global 500|''Fortune'' Global 500]] list (2020).{{cite web |url=https://fortune.com/global500/2020/search/?name=boeing |title=Boeing |website=Fortune |language=en-US |access-date=September 26, 2020 |archive-date=November 16, 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211116191448/https://fortune.com/global500/2020/search/?name=boeing |url-status=live}}

'''Bourgogne-Franche-Comté''' ({{IPA|fr|buʁɡɔɲ fʁɑ̃ʃ kɔ̃te|lang|LL-Q150 (fra)-WikiLucas00-Bourgogne-Franche-Comté.wav}}; {{lit|Burgundy-Free County}}, sometimes abbreviated '''BFC'''; [[Franco-Provençal|Arpitan]]: ''Borgogne-Franche-Comtât'') is a [[Regions of France|region]] in France created by the 2014 territorial reform of French regions, from a merger of [[Burgundy]] and [[Franche-Comté]]. The new region came into existence on 1 January 2016, after the [[2015 French regional elections|regional elections of December 2015]], electing 100 members to the [[Regional Council of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.lemonde.fr/politique/article/2014/12/17/la-carte-a-13-regions-definitivement-adoptee_4542278_823448.html |title=La carte à 13 régions définitivement adoptée |trans-title=The 13-region map finally adopted |newspaper=[[Le Monde]] |agency=[[Agence France-Presse]] |language=fr |date=17 December 2014 |access-date=13 January 2015}}</ref>

The region covers an area of {{convert|47783|km2|abbr=on}} and eight [[Departments of France|departments]]; it had a population of 2,811,423 in 2017.<ref name="Population">{{cite web |url=https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/1405599?geo=REG-27 |title=Comparateur de territoire: Région de Bourgogne-Franche-Comté (27) |work=[[Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques|Insee]] |access-date=11 September 2020}}</ref> It stretches from the border with [[Île-de-France]] in the northwest to the Swiss border in the southeast and from the border with [[Alsace]] in the northeast to the border with [[Beaujolais (province)|Beaujolais]] in the south. It encompasses the [[Morvan]], a large part of the [[Jura Mountains|Jura]] and a small part of the [[Vosges]]. 

Its [[Prefectures in France|prefecture]] and largest city is [[Dijon]], although the [[Regional council (France)|regional council]] sits in [[Besançon]], making Bourgogne-Franche-Comté one of two regions in France (along with [[Normandy (administrative region)|Normandy]]) in which the [[Prefect (France)|prefect]] does not sit in the same city as the regional council.

'''Brasschaat''' ({{IPA|nl|brɑˈsxaːt|-|Nl-Brasschaat.ogg}}) is a [[Municipalities in Belgium|municipality]] located in [[Flemish Region|Flanders]], one of the three regions of [[Belgium]], and in the [[Flanders|Flemish]] [[Provinces of Belgium|province]] of [[Antwerp (province)|Antwerp]]. '''Bursaspor Kulübü Derneği''', commonly known as '''Bursaspor''', is a [[Turkey|Turkish]] professional sports club based in the city of [[Bursa]] that plays in the [[TFF First League]], the second tier of the [[Turkish football league system]]. Founded in 1963, the club has a rich history in [[Football in Turkey|Turkish football]]. Bursaspor's traditional colors are green and white, and the team's home kits typically feature these colors in a striped pattern. The club has played its home matches at the Bursa [[Centennial Atatürk Stadium]] since 2015.

Bursaspor claimed its first-ever [[Süper Lig]] championship in the [[2009–10 Süper Lig]] with 75 points, beating runner-up [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] by just one point.<ref name="goal.com">{{cite web |date=16 May 2010 |title=Bursaspor Pip Fenerbahce To Turkcell Super Lig Title – Goal.com |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/467/turkey/2010/05/16/1927945/bursaspor-pip-fenerbahce-to-turkcell-super-lig-title}}</ref><ref name="Yeşil devrim">[http://www.aksam.com.tr/2010/05/17/haber/spor/6763/yesil_devrim.html Yeşil devrim] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100520004553/http://www.aksam.com.tr/2010/05/17/haber/spor/6763/yesil_devrim.html|date=20 May 2010}} {{in lang|tr}}</ref>  Bursaspor became the second Süper Lig champion not from Istanbul after [[Trabzonspor]] victory in [[1975–76 1.Lig|1975–76 season]].<ref name="Şampiyon Bursaspor!">Bursaspor was also the first club outside Istanbul to win the Süper Lig in 26 years as Trabzonspor's last league title came in 1984.[http://www.zaman.com.tr/haber.do?haberno=984912&title=sampiyon-bursaspor Şampiyon Bursaspor!] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100518101807/http://www.zaman.com.tr/haber.do?haberno=984912&title=sampiyon-bursaspor|date=18 May 2010}} {{in lang|tr}}</ref> This championship brought an end to the era when the "Big Three" teams of Istanbul dominated the Süper Lig competition.

In domestic cup competitions, Bursaspor has also enjoyed notable success. The club has won the [[Turkish Cup]] once (1986), finished runners-up on multiple occasions, and has claimed the [[Prime Minister's Cup (Turkey)|Prime Minister's Cup]] twice. In addition, Bursaspor has twice won promotion from the [[TFF 1. Lig|TFF First League]] (second tier), and has a strong tradition of youth development, having produced several prominent Turkish players over the decades.

Bursaspor's first, and most successful, foray into [[UEFA competitions|European competition]] came in the [[1974–75 European Cup Winners' Cup|1974–75 European Cup Winners’ Cup]], where the team reached the quarter-finals.<ref name="euro">[http://www.bursaspor.org.tr/avrupa.asp AVRUPADA KUPALARI] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110206004130/http://www.bursaspor.org.tr/avrupa.asp|date=6 February 2011}} bursaspor.org.tr {{in lang|tr}}, retrieved 11 May 2010</ref> They also participated in the [[1986–87 UEFA Cup]], the [[1995 UEFA Intertoto Cup]], and the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League]], where they played in the group stages against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. While they finished bottom of their group, qualifying for the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] was a historic achievement for the club and its supporters.

'''Burundi''',{{efn|{{IPAc-en|audio=En-Burundi-pronunciation.ogg|b|ə|ˈ|r|ʊ|n|d|i}} {{respell|bə|RUUN|dee}} or {{IPAc-en|b|ə|ˈ|r|ʌ|n|d|i}} {{respell|bə|RUN|dee}}}} officially the '''Republic of July 2018 |access-date=17 May 2022 |archive-date=16 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220616022648/https://www.presidence.gov.bi/2018/07/03/6271/ |url-status=live}} {{IPA|rn|u.βu.ɾǔː.ndi|}}; {{Langx|sw|Jamuhuri ya Burundi}} {{IPA|sw|ɓuˈruⁿdi||Sw-ke-Burundi.flac}}; {{Langx|fr|République du Burundi}} {{IPA|fr|buʁundi, byʁyndi|}}}} is a [[landlocked country]] in [[East Africa]]. It is located in the [[Great Rift Valley]] at the junction between the [[African Great Lakes]] region and southeastern Africa, with a population of over 14 million people.{{Cite web |title=Burundi Population (2024) – Worldometer |url=https://www.worldometers.info/world-population/burundi-population/ |access-date=2024-10-23 |website=www.worldometers.info |language=en}} It is bordered by [[Rwanda]] to the north, [[Tanzania]] to the east and southeast, and the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] to the west; [[Lake Tanganyika]] lies along its southwestern border. The political [[capital city]] is [[Gitega]] and the economic capital and largest city is [[Bujumbura]].{{cite web |date=13 February 2019 |title=Loi n°1/04 du 04 février 2019 portant Fixation de la Capitale Politique et de la Capitale Economique du Burundi |trans-title=Law No. 1/04 of February 4, 2019, establishing the Political Capital and the Economic Capital of Burundi |url=https://www.presidence.gov.bi/2019/02/13/loi-n104-du-04-fevrier-2019-portant-fixation-de-la-capitale-politique-et-de-la-capitale-economique-du-burundi/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190225103031/https://www.presidence.gov.bi/2019/02/13/loi-n104-du-04-fevrier-2019-portant-fixation-de-la-capitale-politique-et-de-la-capitale-economique-du-burundi/ |archive-date=25 February 2019 |access-date=24 February 2019}} The [[Great Lakes Twa|Twa]], [[Hutu]], and [[Tutsi]] peoples have lived in Burundi for at least 500 years. For more than 200 of those years, Burundi was an independent [[Kingdom of Burundi|kingdom]]. In 1885, it became part of [[German East Africa]].{{cite book |first=Helmut |last=Strizek |title=Geschenkte Kolonien: Ruanda und Burundi unter deutscher Herrschaft |trans-title=Donated colonies: Rwanda and Burundi under German rule |location=Berlin |publisher=Ch. Links Verlag |year=2006 |isbn=978-3-86153-390-0}} After the [[World War I|First World War]] and [[German revolution of 1918–1919|Germany's defeat]], the [[League of Nations]] mandated the territories of Burundi and Rwanda to Belgium in a combined territory called [[Ruanda-Urundi]]. After the [[World War II|Second World War]], this transformed into a [[United Nations trust territories|United Nations trust territory]]. Burundi gained independence in 1962 and initially retained the monarchy. However, a [[July 1966 Burundian coup d'état|coup d'état in 1966]] replaced the monarchy with a [[one-party state|one-party]] republic, and for the next 27 years, Burundi was ruled by a series of ethnic Tutsi dictators and notably experienced a [[Ikiza|genocide of its Hutu population]] in 1972. In 1993, [[Melchior Ndadaye]] became Burundi's first Hutu president following the country's [[1993 Burundian presidential election|first multi-party presidential election]]. His assassination three months later during [[1993 Burundian coup attempt|a coup attempt]] provoked the 12-year [[Burundian Civil War]]. In 2000, the Arusha Agreement was adopted, which was largely integrated in a new constitution in 2005. Since the 2005 post-war elections, the dominant party has been the Hutu-led [[National Council for the Defense of Democracy – Forces for the Defense of Democracy]] (CNDD–FDD), widely accused of authoritarian governance and perpetuating the country's [[Human rights in Burundi|poor human rights record]]. Burundi remains primarily a rural society, with just 13.4% of the population living in urban areas in 2019.{{Citation |title=Burundi |date=2024-01-31 |work=The World Factbook |url=https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/burundi/ |access-date=2024-02-05 |publisher=Central Intelligence Agency |language=en |archive-date=22 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122232849/https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/burundi/ |url-status=dead }} Burundi is densely populated, and many young people emigrate in search of opportunities elsewhere. Roughly 81% of the population are of Hutu origin, 18% are Tutsi, and fewer than 1% are Twa.[[#Eggers|Eggers]], p. ix. The official languages are [[Kirundi language|Kirundi]], French, and English—Kirundi being officially recognised as the sole national language.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2OA9DQAAQBAJ&q=langues+officielles+au+burundi+kirundi+fran%C3%A7ais+anglais&pg=PA104 |title=Les approches bi-plurilingues d'enseignement-apprentissage: autour du programme Écoles et langues nationales en Afrique (ELAN-Afrique): Actes du colloque du 26–27 mars 2015, Université Paul-Valéry, Montpellier, France |first=Sous la direction de Bruno |last=Maurer |date=1 October 2016 |publisher=Archives contemporaines |isbn=978-2-8130-0195-5 |via=Google Books |access-date=10 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180410203233/https://books.google.com/books?id=2OA9DQAAQBAJ&lpg=PA104&ots=tFzjIGhvwU&dq=langues+officielles+au+burundi+kirundi+fran%C3%A7ais+anglais&hl=ru&pg=PA104 |archive-date=10 April 2018 |url-status=live}} One of the smallest countries in Africa, Burundi's land is used mostly for [[subsistence agriculture]] and grazing. [[Deforestation]], [[soil erosion]], and [[habitat loss]] are major ecological concerns.Bermingham, Eldredge, Dick, Christopher W. and Moritz, Craig (2005). ''Tropical Rainforests: Past, Present, and Future''. Chicago, Illinois: University of Chicago Press, p. 146. {{ISBN|0-226-04468-8}} {{As of|2005}}, the country was almost completely deforested. Less than 6% of its land was covered by trees, with over half of that being for commercial plantations.{{Cite web|url=https://rainforests.mongabay.com/20burundi.htm|title=Burundi|last=Butler|first=Rhett A.|date=2006|website=Mongabay|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060505214856/https://rainforests.mongabay.com/20burundi.htm|archive-date=2006-05-05}} Burundi is the poorest country in the world by [[List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita|nominal GDP per capita]] and is one of the [[least developed countries]].{{Cite report |url=https://hdr.undp.org/data-center/specific-country-data |title=Specific country data: Burundi |author=United Nations |date=May 5, 2025 |publisher=United Nations |issue=Human Development Reports |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=GDP per capita |url=https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-worldbank |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509123307/https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-worldbank |archive-date=2026-05-09 |access-date=2026-05-21 |website=Our World in Data |language=en}} It faces widespread [[List of countries by percentage of population living in poverty|poverty]], [[Corruption Perceptions Index|corruption]], [[List of countries by Fragile States Index|instability]] and authoritarianism. Burundi is a member of the [[African Union]], [[Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa]], [[United Nations]], [[East African Community]], [[Organisation internationale de la Francophonie|OIF]] and the [[Non-Aligned Movement]].

The club competes in [[Liga MX]], the top division of [[Mexican football league system|Mexican football]], and plays its home matches at [[Estadio Hidalgo]]. Founded in 1892 as Pachuca Football Club by workers from the mining company ''Real del Monte y Pachuca'', which had mostly British immigrants ([[Cornish diaspora]]). The club changed its name to Pachuca Athletic Club in 1895, and was later refounded in 1960 as the current franchise. Nicknamed ''Tuzos'', it pays tribute to the history and mining heritage of the club and the city. Domestically, CF Pachuca has won seven Liga MX titles. Internationally, the club has won six [[CONCACAF Champions Cup]] titles, one [[Copa Sudamericana|CONMEBOL Sudamericana]], one [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup#Secondary trophy winners|FIFA Challenger Cup]], one [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup#Secondary trophy winners|FIFA Derby of the Americas]], and one [[North American SuperLiga]]. CF Pachuca reached the [[2024 FIFA Intercontinental Cup final]], and also finished in third place in the [[2017 FIFA Club World Cup]]. Founded in 1922, the club plays in the {{Spanish football updater|Tenerife}}, holding home matches at the [[Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López]], with a 22,824-seat capacity. The traditional home colours are white shirts and blue shorts. Tenerife has a history playing in the top flight of [[La Liga]]. They have been promoted to the top tier on four occasions, including a 10-year stint from [[1989–90 La Liga|1989]] to [[1998–99 La Liga|1999]]. The club managed to finish as high as fifth in the league table on two occasions during that period, which qualified them for the first round of the [[UEFA Cup]]. They most recently played in La Liga in the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10]] season. Being based in the Canary archipelago off the Atlantic coast of Africa, while playing its away games on the Spanish mainland, both the club and rival [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] from [[Gran Canaria]] are two of the most geographically isolated professional clubs. |pattern_sh3 = |pattern_so3 = |leftarm3 = 000000 |body3 = 000000 |rightarm3 = 000000 |shorts3 = CCFF00 |socks3 = 000000 }} '''Fotbal Club CFR 1907 Cluj''', commonly known as '''CFR Cluj''' ({{IPA|ro|t͡ʃefeˌre ˈkluʒ}} or {{IPA|ro|ˌt͡ʃefere ˈkluʒ|}}) or simply '''CFR''', is a Romanian professional [[association football|football]] club based in the city of [[Cluj-Napoca]], [[Cluj County]], that competes in the [[Liga I]]. Founded in 1907 as ''Kolozsvári Vasutas Sport Club'', when [[Transylvania]] was part of [[Austria-Hungary]], the club takes its current name from the [[acronym]] for ''[[Căile Ferate Române]]'' ("Romanian Railways"). CFR Cluj first competed in the Romanian top flight in the [[1946–47 Divizia A|1946–47 season]], but was relegated at the end of the [[1947–48 Divizia A|following campaign]]. Aside from another spell in the top division between 1969 and 1976, the club spent most of the twentieth century in the [[Romanian football league system|lower leagues]]. Following its return to the Liga I in 2004, CFR made its European debut in the [[2005 UEFA Intertoto Cup]], finishing as joint runners-up. With substantial financial backing from then-owner Árpád Pászkány, CFR won its first national championship in the [[2007–08 Liga I|2007–08 season]], ending a 17-year period of dominance by teams based in [[Bucharest]].{{cite news |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19588706 |title=BBC Sport – Champions League: What can Manchester United expect in Cluj? |work=BBC Sport |access-date=3 October 2012 |archive-date=4 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004030327/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19588706 |url-status=live }} It subsequently won further domestic honours and established a regular presence in European competitions. After financial difficulties and a change of ownership in the mid-2010s, CFR embarked on a successful run, claiming five consecutive league titles between [[2017–18 Liga I|2017]] and [[2021–22 Liga I|2022]]. All 17 of its major domestic trophies have come in the twenty-first century, comprising eight Liga I titles, five [[Cupa României]], and four [[Supercupa României]]. In European competitions, the club has reached the group stage of the [[UEFA Champions League]] and [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] three times each, and that of the [[UEFA Europa Conference League|Conference League]] twice. CFR shares a [[Cluj derby|local rivalry]] with [[FC Universitatea Cluj|Universitatea Cluj]], which was considered the city's leading football club before "the White-Burgundies" rose to prominence. CFR also developed rivalries with other Romanian teams, particularly [[FCSB]], with which it has frequently competed for the Liga I title in recent years.

It consists of ten [[volcanic island]]s with a combined land area of about 4,033 square kilometres (1,557 sq mi).{{cite magazine |url=http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2013/12/131212-maps-cabo-verde-cartography-science-cape-verde-africa/ |title=Cape Verde Gets New Name: 5 Things to Know About How Maps Change |author=Tanya Basu |magazine=National Geographic |date=12 December 2013 |access-date=12 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213044150/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2013/12/131212-maps-cabo-verde-cartography-science-cape-verde-africa/ |archive-date=13 December 2013 |url-status=dead}} These islands lie between 600 and 850 kilometres (370 and 530 miles) west of [[Cap-Vert]] (i.e., [[Dakar]]), the westernmost point of continental Africa, after which they are named.{{Cite web |date=2025-10-14 |title=Cabo Verde {{!}} Capital, Map, Language, People, & Portugal {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Cabo-Verde |access-date=2025-10-15 |website=britannica.com}} Cape Verde forms part of the [[Macaronesia]] ecoregion, along with the [[Azores]], the [[Canary Islands]], [[Madeira]] and the [[Savage Islands]]. The archipelago was uninhabited until the 15th century, when [[Portuguese maritime exploration|Portuguese explorers]] settled the islands, establishing one of the first [[Age of Discovery|European settlements]] in the tropics. Its strategic position gave it a significant role in the [[Atlantic slave trade|transatlantic slave trade]] during the 16th and 17th centuries; the islands saw rapid economic growth driven by the trade of manufactured goods, rum, cloth for African slaves, ivory, and gold. By the mid 19th century, increased foreign competition, persistent drought, and the decline of the slave trade led to economic decline and emigration; Cape Verde gradually recovered as an important commercial centre and stopping point for major shipping routes. Cape Verde became independent in 1975. Since the early 1990s, it has been a stable [[representative democracy]] and has remained one of the most developed and democratic countries in Africa. Lacking natural resources, its developing economy is mostly service-oriented, with a growing focus on tourism and foreign investment. With a population of around 530,000{{Cite web |title=Total Population by Sex {{!}} United Nations Population Division Data Portal |url=https://population.un.org/dataportal/data/indicators/49/locations/132/start/2026/end/2026/table/pivotbylocation?df=6fda6724-9286-4f19-a8f6-d28cd33907ed |access-date=2026-06-21 |work=United Nations Population Division Data Portal}} ({{As of|2026|lc=y}}), Cape Verde is [[List of African countries by population|among the least populous countries in Africa]]. The Cape Verdean people trace their ancestry primarily to West African populations, with additional contributions from early Portuguese settlers and other groups who came to the islands. A sizeable [[Cape Verdean diaspora|diaspora]] exists across the world, especially in the United States and Portugal, considerably outnumbering the inhabitants on the islands. Cape Verde is a member state of the [[African Union]]. The official language is [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]], while the recognized [[national language]] is [[Cape Verdean Creole]] (Crioulo), which is spoken by the vast majority of the population. As of the 2021 census, the most populous islands were [[Santiago, Cape Verde|Santiago]] (269,370) – which hosts the country's capital and largest city, [[Praia]]; [[São Vicente, Cape Verde|São Vicente]] (74,016); [[Santo Antão, Cape Verde|Santo Antão]] (36,632); [[Fogo, Cape Verde|Fogo]] (33,519); and [[Sal, Cape Verde|Sal]] (33,347). The largest cities are Praia (137,868), [[Mindelo]] (69,013), [[Espargos]] (24,500) and [[Assomada]] (21,297).{{Cite web |title=Cape Verde: Islands, Municipalities, Cities & Urban Localities – Population Statistics, Maps, Charts, Weather and Web Information |url=http://www.citypopulation.de/en/capeverde/ |access-date=2024-02-07 |website=www.citypopulation.de}}

Retrieved 28 January 2009. | calling_code = [[+236]] | iso3166code = CF | cctld = [[.cf]] | ethinc_groups_year = | today = }} The '''Central African Republic'''{{efn|{{bulleted list|{{langx|sg|Ködörösêse tî Bêafrîka}}, {{IPA|sg|kōdōrōsésè tí bé.àfríkà}}|{{langx|fr|République centrafricaine}}, {{IPA|fr|ʁepyblik sɑ̃tʁafʁikɛn|IPA}}; abbreviated '''RCA''' or '''{{lang|fr|Centrafrique}}''', {{IPA|fr|sɑ̃tʁafʁik|}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nationsonline.org/oneworld/central_african_republic.htm|title=Central African Republic – CAR – Country Profile – Nations Online Project|website=www.nationsonline.org|access-date=28 October 2020|archive-date=5 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201105231847/https://www.nationsonline.org/oneworld/central_african_republic.htm|url-status=live}}}}}} ('''CAR''') is a [[landlocked country]] in [[Central Africa]]. It is bordered by [[Chad]] to [[Central African Republic–Chad border|the north]], [[Sudan]] to [[Central African Republic–Sudan border|the northeast]], [[South Sudan]] to [[Central African Republic–South Sudan border|the east]], the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] to [[Central African Republic–Democratic Republic of the Congo border|the south]], the [[Republic of the Congo]] to [[Central African Republic–Republic of the Congo border|the southwest]], and [[Cameroon]] to [[Cameroon–Central African Republic border|the west]]. The CAR covers a land area of about {{convert|620000|km2|sqmi}}. As of 2024, it has a population of 5,357,744, consisting of about 80 ethnic groups.{{citation |last=Mudge |first=Lewis |title=World Report 2019: Rights Trends in Central African Republic |date=11 December 2018 |work= |url=https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2019/country-chapters/central-african-republic |access-date=13 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530235536/https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2019/country-chapters/central-african-republic |archive-date=30 May 2019 |chapter=Central African Republic: Events of 2018}} Having been a French colony under the name [[Ubangi-Shari]],{{efn|{{langx|fr|Oubangui-Chari}}}} [[Sango language|Sango]] is its national language and was also its [[official language|co-official language]] alongside [[French language|French]].{{cite news |date=20 April 2011 |title=Central African Republic country profile |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-13150040 |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=BBC News |language=en-GB}} Its capital and largest city is [[Bangui]], which sits on the country's southern border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The CAR mainly consists of Sudano-Guinean [[savanna]], but also includes a [[Sahel]]o-[[East Sudanian savanna|Sudanian]] zone in the north and an [[Northern Congolian forest–savanna mosaic|equatorial forest zone]] in the south. Two-thirds of the country is within the basin of the [[Ubangi River]] (a tributary of the [[Congo River]]), while the remaining third lies in the basin of the [[Chari River]], which flows into [[Lake Chad]]. The region has been inhabited since at least 8000 BCE. The borders were established by France, which began annexing portions to the [[French Congo]] in the late 19th century and in 1903 established the separate colony of Ubangi-Shari, part of [[French Equatorial Africa]]. After gaining independence from France in 1960, the CAR was ruled by a series of autocratic leaders, including [[Jean-Bédel Bokassa]], who changed the country's name to the [[Central African Empire]] and ruled as a monarch from 1976 to 1979.[https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/dec/03/jean-bedel-bokassa-posthumous-pardon 'Cannibal' dictator Bokassa given posthumous pardon] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170301025416/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/dec/03/jean-bedel-bokassa-posthumous-pardon |date=1 March 2017}}. ''The Guardian''. 3 December 2010 The [[Central African Bush War]] began in 2004 and, despite a peace treaty in 2007 and another in 2011, [[Central African Republic Civil War|civil war resumed]] in 2012. The civil war perpetuated the country's poor [[Human rights in the Central African Republic|human rights record]], characterized by widespread and increasing abuses by various participating armed groups. Despite its vast [[natural resources]], such as [[uranium]] reserves, [[crude oil]], [[gold]], [[diamond]]s, [[cobalt]], [[lumber]], and [[hydropower]], as well as significant quantities of [[arable land]], the CAR is among the world's ten poorest countries, with the world's lowest [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] per capita at purchasing power parity (PPP) as of parties in Sweden|political party in Sweden]], founded in 1913. The party focuses on the [[Economy|national economy]], the [[Natural environment|environment]], political [[Decentralization|decentralisation]] and [[social integration]]. It is represented in all of the [[Riksdag]]'s parliamentary committees, currently holding 25 seats.{{Cite web |date=28 September 2026 |title=Valresultat 2026 – riksdag, region och kommun |url=https://www.val.se/valresultat-och-statistik/riksdags--region--och-kommunval/valresultat-2026 |access-date=5 October 2026 |website=[[Election Authority (Sweden)|Swedish Election Authority]]|language=Swedish|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261019211400/https://www.val.se/valresultat-och-statistik/riksdags--region--och-kommunval/valresultat-2026|archive-date=19 October 2026}} Traditionally part of the [[Nordic agrarian parties|Nordic agrarian]] family of political parties, the Centre Party has increasingly switched focus towards [[economic liberalism]], [[environmental protection]], [[gender equality|equality of the sexes]] and [[Decentralization|decentralisation]] of governmental authority.{{cite news|url=https://sverigesradio.se/sida/artikel.aspx?programid=2054&artikel=5933041|title=The Centre Party – Centerpartiet|newspaper=[[Sveriges Radio]]|date=7 August 2014|access-date=28 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126195421/https://sverigesradio.se/sida/artikel.aspx?programid=2054&artikel=5933041|archive-date=26 January 2016|url-status=live}}{{cite book|author1=Carina Bischoff|author2=Marlene Wind|author-link2=Marlene Wind|chapter=Sweden|editor=Donatella M. Its environmental policies stress the importance of consent and voluntary action,{{Cite web|title=Biologisk mångfald|url=https://www.centerpartiet.se/var-politik/politik-a-o/miljo/biologisk-mangfald|url-status=live|access-date=27 November 2021|website=Centre Party|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801202519/https://www.centerpartiet.se/var-politik/politik-a-o/miljo/biologisk-mangfald |archive-date=1 August 2018 }} including working with [[forester]]s and private landowners to promote [[biodiversity]] within a mutually agreeable framework.{{Cite web|title=Engagerade privata skogsägare har skapat mångfalden i skogen – inte trädkramarna|url=https://www.allehanda.se/2021-11-20/engagerade-privata-skogsagare-har-skapat-mangfalden-i-skogen--inte-tradkramarna|access-date=2021-11-27|website=Allehanda.se|date=20 November 2021|language=sv|archive-date=27 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127105805/https://www.allehanda.se/2021-11-20/engagerade-privata-skogsagare-har-skapat-mangfalden-i-skogen--inte-tradkramarna|url-status=live}} The Centre Party has produced two [[Prime Minister of Sweden|prime ministers of Sweden]]: [[Axel Pehrsson-Bramstorp|Axel Pehrsson]] who held the prime minister post for three months in 1936 and [[Thorbjörn Fälldin]] who held the post for a total of five years, from [[Fälldin I cabinet|1976 to 1978]] and then again from [[Fälldin II cabinet|1979]] to [[Fälldin III cabinet|1982]]. It is a member of the [[Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe Party|Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe]], the [[Liberal International]] and [[Renew Europe]]. It was originally named the '''Farmers' League''' ({{langx|sv|link=no|Bondeförbundet}} {{IPA|sv|ˈbʊ̂nːdɛfœrˌbɵndɛt||Sv-Bondeförbundet.ogg}}; '''B''').

([[Chairman#Public corporations|chairman]] and CEO){{cite web|last1=DiChristopher|first1=Tom|title=Chevron names Mike Wirth chairman and CEO|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/09/28/chevron-names-michael-wirth-chairman-and-ceo.html|website=MSNBC|date=September 28, 2017|access-date=February 15, 2018}} | industry = {{ubl|[[Energy industry|Energy]]|[[Petroleum industry|Oil and gas]]}} | products = [[Gasoline]], [[natural gas]] and other [[petrochemical]]s | revenue = {{nowrap| {{increase}} {{US$|202.7 billion|link=yes}} (2024)}} | operating_income = {{decrease}} {{US$|18.72 billion}} (2024) | net_income = {{decrease}} {{US$|17.66 billion}} (2024) | assets = {{decrease}} {{US$|256.9 billion}} (2024) | equity = {{decrease}} {{US$|152.3 billion}} (2024) | num_employees = 45,298 (2024) | hq_location = [[Houston]], Texas, U.S. | owner = [[Berkshire Hathaway]] (6.70%) | parent = | subsidiaries = {{plainlist| * [[Chevron Phillips Chemical]] (50%) * [[Chevron Lubricants Lanka]] (51%) }} | brands = {{plainlist| * Chevron * [[Texaco]] * [[Caltex]] * [[Havoline]] * [[Hess Corporation|Hess]] * [[Techron]] * [[gear oil|RPM]] * [[gear oil|Delo]] * Calso (1946–55) * [[Gulf Oil|Gulf]] (1985–2010) }} | website = {{URL|https://www.chevron.com/|chevron.com}} | footnotes = {{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/0000093410/000009341025000009/cvx-20241231.htm |title=2024 Annual Report (Form 10-K) |publisher=[[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] |date=February 21, 2025}}[https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/0000093410/000119312526145617/d77994ddef14a.htm#toc77994_45 2026 Proxy Statement] }} '''Chevron Corporation''' is an American multinational [[List of oil exploration and production companies|energy corporation]] predominantly specializing in [[Petroleum industry|oil and gas]]. The second-largest [[Successors of Standard Oil|direct descendant of Standard Oil]], and originally known as the '''Standard Oil Company of California''' (shortened to '''Socal''' or '''CalSo'''), it is active in more than 180 countries. Founded originally in [[Southern California]] during the 1870s. After the [[Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey v. United States|breakup of Standard Oil]], Socal grew quickly on its own by continuing to acquire companies and partnering with others both inside and outside of California, eventually becoming one of the [[Big Oil]] companies that dominated the global petroleum industry from the mid-1940s to the 1970s. In 1985, Socal merged with the Pittsburgh-based [[Gulf Oil]] and rebranded as Chevron; the newly merged company later merged with [[Texaco]] in 2001.{{Cite web |title=Chevron History |url=https://www.chevron.com/about/history |access-date=September 1, 2022 |website=chevron.com |language=en-us}} Chevron is one of the largest companies in the world and the second-largest oil company based in the United States by revenue, only behind fellow Standard Oil descendant [[ExxonMobil]]. Within oil and gas, Chevron is [[Vertical integration|vertically integrated]] and is involved in [[hydrocarbon exploration]], [[Petroleum#Extraction|production]], [[refining]], marketing and transport, chemicals manufacturing and sales, and [[power generation]]. Chevron manufactures and sells fuels, lubricants, additives, and petrochemicals, primarily in [[Western North America]], the US [[Gulf Coast of the United States|Gulf Coast]], Southeast Asia, South Korea and Australia. In 2018, the company produced an average of {{convert|791000|oilbbl|m3}} of net oil-equivalent per day in United States.{{Cite web |title=United States Highlights of Operations |url=https://www.chevron.com/worldwide/united-states |access-date=April 2, 2020 |website=chevron.com |language=en-us}} Chevron ranked 10th on the [[Fortune 500|''Fortune'' 500]] in 2023. The company is also the last-remaining oil-and-gas component of the [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] since the exit of [[ExxonMobil]] from the index in 2020.{{Cite web |title=Check out Chevron Corp's stock price (CVX) in real time |url=https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/CVX |access-date=August 15, 2022 |website=CNBC |date=January 29, 2012 |language=en}}{{Cite news |title=Chevron: 2022 Fortune 500 |url=https://fortune.com/company/chevron/fortune500/ |access-date=August 15, 2022 |website=Fortune |language=en}} Chevron has been subject to [[Criticism of Chevron|numerous controversies]] relating to its activities involving [[climate change]]. In particular, one of its most widely covered incidents on social media was its continued denial of ecological damage near the [[Lago Agrio oil field]] and its involvements against [[Steven Donziger]], a controversy rooted and inherited from [[Texaco]] when Chevron acquired it in 2001. Chevron has also received negative attention for numerous other oil extraction projects, especially within the Los Angeles metropolitan area and in the Eastern Mediterranean. In 2024, Chevron was responsible for 512 Mt of CO2 emissions, which was 1.33% of global CO2 emissions.{{Cite web |last=InfluenceMap |title=Carbon Majors: 2024 Data Update |url=https://carbonmajors.org/briefing/Carbon-Majors-2024-Data-Update-35466 |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=carbonmajors.org |language=en}}

'''Chhattisgarh''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|tʃ|æ|t|ɪ|s|ɡ|ɑː|r}}; {{IPA|hi|ˈtʃʰət̪ːiːsgəɽʱ|lang}}) is a landlocked [[States and union territories of India|state]] in [[Eastern India|east]]-[[central India]].{{Cite web|title=Chhattisgarh|url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Chhattisgarh|website=Britannica|access-date=16 January 2026}} It is the [[List of states and union territories of India by area|ninth largest state by area]], and with a population of roughly 30 million, the [[List of states and union territories of India by population|seventeenth most populous]].{{Cite web|title=Chhattisgarh Population 2020/2021|url=https://www.populationu.com/in/chhattisgarh-population|access-date=22 August 2021|website=www.populationu.com|archive-date=11 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411061048/https://www.populationu.com/in/chhattisgarh-population|url-status=dead}} It borders seven states – [[Uttar Pradesh]] to the north, [[Madhya Pradesh]] to the northwest, [[Maharashtra]] to the southwest, [[Jharkhand]] to the northeast, [[Odisha]] to the east, [[Andhra Pradesh]] and [[Telangana]] to the south.{{cite web|url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/Chhattisgarh,+India/|title=Google Maps|publisher=Google Maps|access-date=6 December 2015|archive-date=31 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531185712/https://www.google.com/maps/place/Chhattisgarh,+India/|url-status=live}} Formerly a part of [[Madhya Pradesh]], it was granted statehood on [[Chhattisgarh Rajyotsava|1 November 2000]] with [[Raipur]] as the designated state capital.{{cite web |url=http://cgfinance.nic.in/Rules%20%26%20Act/Reorganisation%20Act-2000/Reorganisation%20Act%2C2000%28English%29.PDF |title=Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000 |access-date=29 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130718013901/http://cgfinance.nic.in/Rules%20%26%20Act/Reorganisation%20Act-2000/Reorganisation%20Act%2C2000%28English%29.PDF |archive-date=18 July 2013 |url-status=dead }} The [[Jogimara and Sitabenga Caves|Sitabenga Caves]] in Chhattisgarh, one of the earliest examples of theatre architecture in India, are dated to the [[Maurya Empire|Mauryan period]] of 3rd century BCE. The region was split between rivaling dynasties from the sixth to twelfth centuries, and parts of it were briefly under the [[Chola dynasty]] in the 11th century. Eventually, most of Chhattisgarh was consolidated under the [[Kingdom of Haihaiyavansi]], whose rule lasted for 700 years until they were brought under Maratha suzerainty in 1740. The [[Bhonsles of Nagpur]] incorporated Chhattisgarh into the [[Kingdom of Nagpur]] in 1758 and ruled until 1845, when the region was annexed by the [[East India Company]], and was later administered under the [[British Raj|Raj]] until 1947 as the [[Chhattisgarh Division]] of the [[Central Provinces]]. Some areas constituting present-day Chhattisgarh were [[princely state]]s that were later merged into Madhya Pradesh. The [[States Reorganisation Act, 1956]] placed Chhattisgarh in Madhya Pradesh, and it remained a part of that state for 44 years. Chhattisgarh is one of the fastest-developing states in India.{{cite web|title=Chhattisgarh Steel |url=http://india.gov.in/knowindia/st_chhattisgarh.php |access-date=22 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110707025600/http://india.gov.in/knowindia/st_chhattisgarh.php |archive-date=7 July 2011 }} Its [[Gross regional domestic product|Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP)]] is {{INRConvert|5.09|lc}} (2023–24 est.), with a [[per capita]] GSDP of {{INRConvert|152348|lk=r}} (2023–24 est.). A resource-rich state, it has the third largest [[coal]] reserves in the country and provides electricity, coal, and steel to the rest of the nation.{{cite web|url=https://coal.gov.in/major-statistics/coal-reserves|title=Coal reserves|access-date=26 May 2022|archive-date=30 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330013125/https://coal.gov.in/major-statistics/coal-reserves|url-status=live}}{{cite web|title=Chhattisgarh State – Power Hub |url=http://cg.gov.in/power/power1.htm |access-date=22 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101120182905/http://cg.gov.in/power/power1.htm |archive-date=20 November 2010 }} It also has the third largest forest cover in the country after [[Madhya Pradesh]] and [[Arunachal Pradesh]] with over 41.21% of the state covered by forests.

'''Chiayi''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|dʒ|j|ɑː|ˈ|iː}}),<ref>{{Cite Merriam-Webster|Chia-i}}</ref> officially known as '''Chiayi City''',{{efn native lang|tw|name=word1|t=嘉義市|p=Jiāyì Shì|m=Ka-gī-tshī}} is a [[Provincial city (Taiwan)|city]] located in [[Chianan Plain]] in [[Regions of Taiwan|southwestern Taiwan]], surrounded by [[Chiayi County]] with a population of 263,188 inhabitants as of January 2023.

The [[Hoanya people]] inhabited present-day Chiayi under its historical name of ''Tirosen'' prior to the arrival of [[Han Chinese]] in Taiwan and was ruled by the [[Dutch Formosa|Dutch]] and the [[Kingdom of Tungning]] under various names. During the [[Taiwan under Qing rule|Qing dynasty]], Tirosen was governed as part of [[Taiwan Prefecture]] in [[Fuchien Province, Republic of China|Fujian]] under [[Zhuluo County]] and the city was renamed '''Kagee''' in 1787. The city adopted the Japanese reading '''Kagi''' during the [[Taiwan under Japanese rule|Japanese era]]. Soon afterwards an [[1906 Meishan earthquake|earthquake in 1906]] destroyed much of the town. Kagi was administered as part of [[Tainan Prefecture]] from 1920 onwards. Following the [[surrender of Japan]] in 1945, the [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]], who [[1911 Revolution|deposed the Qing in 1911]], took control of the city (which from then on was rendered as '''Chiayi''' City, following the Chinese pronunciation) and administered it as a provincial city of [[Taiwan (Republic of China province)|Taiwan Province]] before being integrated into Chiayi County in 1950 as a [[county-administered city]]. The city was restored to its status as a provincial city in 1982. In 1998, Taiwan Province was streamlined and Chiayi City has been governed directly since then by the [[Executive Yuan]].

The city is known for [[Alishan National Scenic Area]] and warm [[humid subtropical climate]] in the summer months. Left with the landmarks of Japanese colonial rule, Chiayi City has the round-island railway system and [[Alishan Forest Railway]] where the city is the starting point along with various Japanese temples.

'''Chicago Bulls''' are an American professional [[basketball]] team based in [[Chicago]]. The Bulls compete in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) as a member of the [[Central Division (NBA)|Central Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]]. The team was founded on January 16, 1966, and played its first game during the [[1966–67 Chicago Bulls season|1966–67 NBA season]].{{cite web|title=This Date in the NBA–January |url=https://www.nba.com/news/history-this-date-in-nba-jan#/|publisher=NBA Media Ventures, LLC|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171219204233/http://www.nba.com/history/this-date-jan#/|archive-date=December 19, 2017|url-status=live}} The Bulls share their home arena with the [[National Hockey League]]'s [[Chicago Blackhawks]], playing in the newer [[United Center]] which replaced the former [[Chicago Stadium]]. The Bulls saw their greatest success during the 1990s when they played a major part in popularizing the NBA worldwide. They are known for having one of the NBA's greatest dynasties, winning six [[List of NBA champions|NBA championships]] between 1991 and 1998 with two separate [[three-peat]]s. All six of their championship teams were led by Hall of Famers [[Michael Jordan]], [[Scottie Pippen]] and coach [[Phil Jackson]]. The Bulls are the only NBA team to win multiple championships while never losing an [[NBA Finals]] series in their history.{{cite book|last=Jozsa|first=J. P. Jr.|year=2015|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=H02qBAAAQBAJ|title=National Basketball Association Strategies: Business Expansions, Relocations, and Mergers|location=Berlin/Heidelberg|publisher=Springer|page=[https://books.google.com/books?id=H02qBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA11 11]|isbn=978-3-319-10058-6 |access-date=April 19, 2025}} The Bulls won 72 games during the [[1995–96 NBA season|1995–96 season]], setting an [[List of NBA regular season records|NBA record]] that stood until the [[Golden State Warriors]] won 73 games during the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]]. The Bulls were the first team in NBA history to win 70 games or more in a single season, and the only NBA franchise to do so until the 2015–16 Warriors.{{cite news |title=Warriors Become Second Team in NBA History to Win 70 Games in a Single Season |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/70-wins-20160407 |publisher=NBA Media Ventures, LLC |website=Warriors.com |date=April 7, 2016 |access-date=December 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223133724/http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/70-wins-20160407|archive-date=December 23, 2016|url-status=live}} Since 1998, the Bulls have failed to regain their former success. The franchise struggled throughout the 2000s but showed promise in the early 2010s led by [[Derrick Rose]] and [[Joakim Noah]], culminating in back-to-back seasons above .732 in [[2010–11 Chicago Bulls season|2010–11]] and [[2011–12 Chicago Bulls season|2011–12]]. An [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] tear suffered by Rose and subsequent trades of key players triggered a rebuild, culminating in different lineups throughout the late 2010s and early 2020s. Jordan and Rose won the [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award]] while playing for the Bulls, for a total of six MVP awards. The Bulls share rivalries with the [[Bulls–Cavaliers rivalry|Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Bulls–Pistons rivalry|Detroit Pistons]], and the [[Bulls–Knicks rivalry|New York Knicks]].

'''China''',{{efn|{{lang-zh|s=中国|p=Zhōngguó}}}} officially the '''People's Republic of China''' ('''PRC'''),{{efn|{{lang-zh|s=中华人民共和国|p=Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó}}}} is a country in [[East Asia]]. It is divided into 33 [[Province-level divisions of China|province-level divisions]], including two [[Special administrative regions of China|special administrative regions]].{{Efn|Not including the ''de jure'' [[Taiwan (People's Republic of China province)|Taiwan Province]], controlled by the [[Republic of China]].{{sfn|Zhao|2023|p=46}}|group=lower-alpha}} [[Beijing]] is the capital, while [[Shanghai]] is the [[List of cities in China by population|most populous city by urban area]]. Its geography features the [[Zhongyuan|Central Plain]], major rivers such as the [[Yangtze]] and [[Yellow River]], deserts, [[subtropical]] and temperate forests, plateaus, and [[mountain range]]s such as the [[Himalayas]]. It is the [[list of countries by population (United Nations)|world's second-most populous country]] after [[India]], with [[population of China|a population]] exceeding 1.4 billion (17% of the world's population). Covering {{Convert|9.6|e6sqkm|sqmi|sp=us}}, it is the [[list of countries and dependencies by area|third largest country by area]].{{efn|name=area|The total area ranking relative to the [[United States]] depends on the measurement of total areas. See [[list of countries and dependencies by area]] for information. The following two primary sources represent the range of estimates of China's and the United States' total areas. # The ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'' lists China as the third-largest country (after Russia and Canada) with a total area of 9,572,900 km{{Sup|2}}. # The [[The World Factbook|CIA ''World Factbook'']] lists China as the fourth-largest country (after Russia, Canada and the United States) with a total area of 9,596,960 km{{Sup|2}}.}} Humans first arrived in China during the [[Paleolithic]]. During the 2nd millennium BCE, [[Dynasties in Chinese history|dynastic states]] emerged. In 221 BCE, China was unified under the [[Qin dynasty|Qin]], followed by the [[Han dynasty]], ushering in two millennia of imperial rule across periods of unity and division. The [[Imperial era of Chinese history|imperial era]] saw the expansion of the [[Silk Road]] and the invention of [[invention of gunpowder|gunpowder]], [[History of paper#Paper in China|paper]], [[printing]], and the [[compass]]. After increased Western political, economic, and philosophical influence, the empire was succeeded by the [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]] (ROC) after the [[1911 Revolution]]. The [[Warlord Era]] and [[Chinese Civil War]] followed, interrupted by the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], which ended in a Chinese victory. In 1949, the [[Chinese Communist Party]] (CCP) [[proclamation of the People's Republic of China|proclaimed the PRC]] and the [[Retreat of the government of the Republic of China to Taiwan|ROC retreated to Taiwan]]. Both sides still claim political legitimacy. Attempts by the CCP to advance [[Maoism|its political program]] faltered through [[Great Chinese Famine|famine]] and political turmoil. The [[reform and opening up|reform and opening-up]] that began in 1978 moved China towards a [[socialist market economy]], spurring economic growth. China is a [[unitary state]] with the CCP as its [[One-party state|sole ruling party]]. It is one of the five [[Permanent members of the United Nations Security Council|permanent members]] of the [[UN Security Council]] and a member of [[International organization membership of China|many multilateral organizations]]. China is the world's [[List of countries by manufacturing output|largest manufacturer]] and has the [[List of countries by GDP (nominal)|second-largest economy by nominal GDP]]. International organizations have criticized China, alleging authoritarianism and [[Human rights in China|human rights abuses]]. Possessing [[People's Liberation Army|a large military]], [[Chinese space program|space program]], and [[Nuclear weapons of China|nuclear stockpile]], China has been described as a [[superpower]] due to its influence in geopolitics, [[Science and technology in China|science and technology]], [[Industry in China|manufacturing]], [[Economy of China|economics]], and [[Chinese culture|culture]]. [[Chinese art]] and culture have [[Sinosphere|influenced much of Asia]], with [[Chinese literature|a literary tradition]] dating back millennia to the [[Chinese classics]]. China is the birthplace of [[Confucianism]] and [[Daoism]], which form the traditional [[three teachings]] of [[Chinese philosophy]] and [[Chinese folk religion|folk religion]] alongside [[Buddhism]]. [[Chinese cuisine]] is diverse and highly regional, with rice as a staple in the south and wheat in the north. It has [[List of World Heritage Sites in China|60 World Heritage Sites]], including the [[Great Wall of China|Great Wall]] and [[Grand Canal (China)|Grand Canal]]. The [[Han Chinese|Han]], speakers of [[Sinitic languages]], are China's dominant ethnicity, although it is home to [[List of ethnic groups in China|55 recognized minorities]], including the [[Hui people|Hui]], [[Mongols]], [[Tibetans]], [[Uyghurs]], and [[Zhuang people|Zhuang]]. {{TOClimit|3}}

The company was formed in 1998 by the merger of Citicorp, the [[bank holding company]] for [[Citibank]], and [[The Travelers Companies|Travelers]]; Travelers was spun off from the company in 2002.{{cite news | last=Martin | first=Mitchell | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/07/news/07iht-citi.t.html | title=Citicorp and Travelers Plan to Merge in Record $70 billion Deal | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=April 7, 1998|access-date=2026-02-27}}{{cite news | url=https://money.cnn.com/2001/12/19/ipo/citigroup/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011227154326/http://money.cnn.com/2001/12/19/ipo/citigroup/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=December 27, 2001 | title=Citigroup to spin Travelers | work=[[CNN]] | date=December 19, 2001}} Citigroup is the [[List of largest banks in the United States|third-largest banking institution]] in the United States by assets; alongside [[JPMorgan Chase]], [[Bank of America]], and [[Wells Fargo]], it is one of the [[Big Four (banking)#United States|Big Four]] banking institutions of the United States.{{cite news | url=https://www.thebalance.com/the-big-4-us-banks-315130 | title=The Biggest Banks in the United States | last=ONeil | first=Erin | work=The Balance | date=August 2, 2016 | access-date=2026-02-27 | archive-date=November 21, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201121174907/https://www.thebalance.com/the-big-4-us-banks-315130 | url-status=dead }} It is considered a [[Systemically important financial institution|systemically important bank]] by the [[Financial Stability Board]] and is commonly called "[[too big to fail]]". It is one of the eight global investment banks in the [[Bulge Bracket]]. Citigroup is ranked 36th on the [[Fortune 500|''Fortune'' 500]],{{cite web | url=https://fortune.com/company/citigroup/fortune500/ | title=Fortune 500: Citigroup | work=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]|access-date=2026-02-27}} and was ranked #24 in [[Forbes Global 2000|''Forbes'' Global 2000]] in 2023.{{Cite web|language=en|url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/global2000/?sh=51d599675ac0|title=The Global 2000 2023|website=Forbes|access-date=2024-02-07|archive-date=2024-01-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240129031905/https://www.forbes.com/lists/global2000/?sh=4f5ab07e5ac0}}The company has assets under management of around US$2.8T{{Cite web |title=Citigroup Total Assets 2012-2026 {{!}} C |url=https://www.macrotrends.net/stocks/charts/C/citigroup/total-assets |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=www.macrotrends.net}}. Citigroup operates across five core businesses:{{cite web |url=https://www.citigroup.com/global/news/press-release/2023/citi-aligns-organizational-structure-strategy-simplifies-operating-model |title=Citi Aligns Organizational Structure with Its Strategy and Simplifies Operating Model |website=Citigroup |date=September 13, 2023 |access-date=2026-09-04}} '''Banking & International''', which provides [[investment banking]], corporate banking, and [[commercial banking]] services; '''Markets''', which provides [[sales and trading]] services; '''Services''' (formerly known as Treasury and Trade Solutions, or TTS), which provides cash management, payments, trade finance, liquidity management, securities services, and [[custodian bank|custody banking]] to corporations, financial institutions, and public-sector clients; '''Wealth''', which comprises Citi's [[wealth management]] and [[retail banking]] businesses{{cite web |title=Citi Announces CFO Transition Plans and Changes to U.S. Personal Banking Business |url=https://www.citigroup.com/global/news/press-release/2025/citi-cfo-transition-plans-changes-united-states-personal-banking-business |website=Citigroup |access-date=2026-09-04}} and includes [[Citibank]]; and '''U.S. Consumer Cards''', which is the third-largest issuer of [[credit card]]s in the United States.{{cite news |url=https://money.usnews.com/credit-cards/articles/biggest-us-credit-card-companies-this-year |title=8 Biggest U.S. Credit Card Companies This Year |first=Ben |last=Luthi |work=[[U.S. News & World Report]] |date=May 2, 2023 |access-date=2026-02-27}}

McBride]] (1944–1953) * [[David Jones (Browns owner)|Dave Jones]] (1953–1961) * [[Art Modell]] (1961–1996) * [[Al Lerner]] (1998–2002) * [[Randy Lerner]] (2002–2012) * '''[[Jimmy Haslam|Jimmy]] & [[Dee Haslam]] (2012–present)''' }} The '''Cleveland Browns''' are a professional [[American football]] team based in [[Cleveland]]. The Browns compete in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) as a member of the [[American Football Conference]] (AFC) [[AFC North|North]] division. The team is named after original coach and co-founder [[Paul Brown]]. They play their home games at [[Huntington Bank Field]], which opened in 1999,{{cite news|last=Florjancic|first=Matt|title=Browns Stadium to become 'FirstEnergy Stadium'|url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-Stadium-to-become-FirstEnergy-Stadium/eebc8394-ae91-4d2d-b7e9-6bf1413e9809|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=January 15, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130117050526/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-Stadium-to-become-FirstEnergy-Stadium/eebc8394-ae91-4d2d-b7e9-6bf1413e9809|archive-date=January 17, 2013|access-date=November 27, 2018|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|last=Naymik|first=Mark|title=Browns owner Jimmy Haslam has spell over football fans and politicians alike|url=http://www.cleveland.com/naymik/index.ssf/2013/03/browns_owner_jimmy_haslam_has.html|newspaper=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=March 8, 2013|access-date=April 1, 2016|archive-date=March 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303222242/http://www.cleveland.com/naymik/index.ssf/2013/03/browns_owner_jimmy_haslam_has.html|url-status=live}} with administrative offices and training facilities in [[Berea, Ohio]] at the [[CrossCountry Mortgage]] campus. The franchise's official club colors are brown, orange, and white.{{cite web|title=New Browns Logo|url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/team/2015_Logos.html|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=February 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150224235956/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/team/2015_Logos.html|archive-date=February 24, 2015|access-date=June 11, 2016|url-status=dead}} They are unique among the 32 member clubs of the NFL in that they do not have a logo on their helmets.{{cite news|last=Gribble|first=Andrew|title=Browns' logos sneak preview of what's to come|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-logos-sneak-preview-of-what-s-to-come-14963233|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=February 24, 2015|access-date=September 5, 2019|archive-date=September 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190905221625/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-logos-sneak-preview-of-what-s-to-come-14963233|url-status=live}}{{cite news|last=Gribble|first=Andrew|title=Putting to rest 5 historic myths about the Browns' uniforms|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/putting-to-rest-5-historic-myths-about-the-browns-uniforms|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=April 2, 2015|access-date=September 5, 2019|archive-date=September 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190905221627/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/putting-to-rest-5-historic-myths-about-the-browns-uniforms-15103110|url-status=live}} The franchise was founded in 1944 by Brown and businessman [[Arthur B. McBride]] as a charter member of the [[All-America Football Conference]] (AAFC), and began play in 1946. The Browns dominated the AAFC, compiling a 47–4–3 record in the league's four seasons and winning its championship in each.{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns-Team history |url=http://www.pigskinacademy.com/Cleveland_Browns.html |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130106120447/http://www.pigskinacademy.com/Cleveland_Browns.html |archive-date=January 6, 2013 |access-date=September 29, 2015 |website=Pigskin Academy}} When the AAFC folded after the 1949 season, the Browns joined the NFL along with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and the [[Baltimore Colts (1947–1950)|original Baltimore Colts]]. The Browns won a championship in [[1950 NFL season|their inaugural NFL season]], as well as in the [[1954 NFL season|1954]], [[1955 NFL season|1955]], and [[1964 NFL season|1964 season]]s, and in a feat unequaled in any of the North American major professional sports, played in their league championship game in each of their first 10 years of existence, winning seven of those games. From 1965 to 1995, they qualified to play in the [[NFL playoffs]] 14 times, but did not win another championship or play in the [[Super Bowl]] during that period.{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns Playoff History |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cle/playoffs.htm |access-date=2024-08-13 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In 1995, owner [[Art Modell]], who had purchased the Browns in 1961, announced plans to move the team to [[Baltimore]]. After threats of legal action from the city of Cleveland and fans, [[Cleveland Browns relocation controversy|a compromise]] was reached in early 1996 that allowed Modell to establish the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as a new franchise while retaining the contracts of all Browns personnel. The Browns' [[intellectual property]], including team name, logos, training facility, and history, were kept [[Trust law|in trust]] and the franchise was regarded by the NFL as suspended, guaranteed to return no later than the 1999 season, either by moving an existing franchise or an expansion draft. While several franchises considered moving to Cleveland, in 1998 it was confirmed that the NFL would hold [[1999 NFL expansion draft|an expansion draft]] and field 31 teams when the Browns resumed play in 1999. Although the 1999 Browns were restocked via an expansion draft, the Browns are not considered to be an [[expansion franchise]].{{Cite news |last=Cabot |first=Mary Kay |date=September 6, 2012 |title=Art Modell's decision to move Cleveland Browns haunted him for rest of life |url=http://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2012/09/art_modell_never_really_recove.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141011172531/http://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2012/09/art_modell_never_really_recove.html |archive-date=October 11, 2014 |access-date=August 25, 2014 |work=[[The Plain Dealer]]}} Since resuming operations in 1999, the Browns have struggled to find success, especially during the 2010s when they failed to post a winning season throughout the decade.{{Cite web |last=D'Andrea |first=Christian |date=December 31, 2019 |title=The defining Browns moment of each year in the 2010s |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2019/12/31/21042675/cleveland-browns-sadness-2010s-decade-draft-busts-coach-firings-quarterbacks |access-date=June 21, 2022 |website=SBNation.com |language=en}} They have had only four winning seasons ([[2002 Cleveland Browns season|2002]], [[2007 Cleveland Browns season|2007]], [[2020 Cleveland Browns season|2020]], and [[2023 Cleveland Browns season|2023]]), three playoff appearances (2002, 2020, and 2023), and one playoff win (2020), winning less than one third of their games in total, and in 2017 were only [[2017 Cleveland Browns season|the second team in NFL history]] to have a 0–16 season after the [[2008 Detroit Lions season|2008 Detroit Lions]]. The franchise has also been noted for a lack of stability with head coaches (10 full time—including two who were fired after only one season—and two interim since 1999) and [[quarterback]]s (42 different starters since 1999).{{cite web |title=Bailey Zappe to start at QB for Browns' season finale in Baltimore, AP source says |url=https://fox8.com/news/bailey-zappe-to-start-at-quarterback-for-browns-season-finale-in-baltimore-ap-source-says/ |website=Fox 8.com |date=January 2, 2025 |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=January 2, 2025}} From 2003 to 2019, the Browns had a 17-season playoff drought, which ended during the [[2020 Cleveland Browns season|2020 season]].{{cite news|last=Gribble|first=Andrew|title=PLAYOFF BOUND! Browns beat Steelers to punch long-awaited postseason ticket|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/playoff-bound-browns-beat-steelers-to-punch-long-awaited-postseason-ticketC|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=January 3, 2021|access-date=January 4, 2021|archive-date=January 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210104000343/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/playoff-bound-browns-beat-steelers-to-punch-long-awaited-postseason-ticket|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |date=2017-10-11 |title=Kevin Hogan will be Browns' 28th starting quarterback since 1999 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/kevin-hogan-will-be-browns-28th-starting-quarterback-since-1999 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171013112755/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/10/11/kevin-hogan-will-be-browns-28th-starting-quarterback-since-1999/ |archive-date=October 13, 2017 |access-date=2024-08-13 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}} They are one of four teams to have never appeared in a Super Bowl. Their lack of recent success has been such that their [[Browns–Steelers rivalry|decades-long rivalry]] with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]—a rivalry in which at one point the Browns had a 22-game lead in the all-time series—saw the Steelers overtake the Browns in the rivalry in 2007 to hold a current 17-game edge over the Browns.
